stories.title: Data centre confusion risks investment pipeline, operators warn
stories.summary: Data centre operators are warning that inconsistent regulatory interpretation and overlapping approval requirements across Australian jurisdictions are creating investment uncertainty and threatening to stall projects in the development pipeline. Industry groups have called for standardized national frameworks to replace the current patchwork of state and local planning rules.
stories.why_it_matters: Regulatory fragmentation directly translates to higher project risk premiums and extended capital lock-up periods, disadvantaging Australia against markets with clearer permitting pathways like Singapore or Malaysia. International developers may redirect planned investment to more predictable jurisdictions, while domestic operators with established government relationships gain relative advantage in navigating complexity.
stories.title_zh: 运营商警告：数据中心政策混乱危及投资管道
stories.summary_zh: 数据中心运营商警告称，澳大利亚各司法管辖区之间不一致的监管解释和重叠的审批要求正在造成投资不确定性，并威胁到开发pipeline中的项目停滞。行业团体呼吁建立标准化的国家框架，以取代当前各州和地方规划规则的拼凑局面。
stories.why_zh: 监管碎片化直接转化为更高的项目风险溢价和延长的资本锁定期，使澳大利亚相对于Singapore或Malaysia等许可路径更清晰的市场处于劣势。国际开发商可能将计划投资转向更可预测的司法管辖区，而拥有既定政府关系的国内运营商在应对复杂性方面获得相对优势。
stories.content:
The Albanese government’s ambiguous stance on data centres is putting Australian investment at risk, industry operators warn, as suburban projects face growing community backlash and mounting political scrutiny.

The federal government is drafting legislation to regulate data centres, weighing up restrictions on major artificial intelligence facilities being built in suburban neighbourhoods.

stories.title: MBSB Research sees potential for 4GW data centre campus at YTL Power's Bukit Kerayong site
stories.summary: MBSB Research has identified potential for a 4GW data centre campus at YTL Power's Bukit Kerayong site in Malaysia, building on the company's existing operations in Kulai and planned expansion into Sedenak Tech Park West. The research note maintains a positive long-term outlook for YTL Power anchored by data centre growth alongside power and digital infrastructure opportunities.
stories.why_it_matters: A 4GW campus would rank among Southeast Asia's largest consolidated data centre developments, concentrating regional AI training capacity and reshaping Johor's competitive position against Singapore. YTL Power's integrated power generation and land assets create a vertically integrated model that threatens standalone data centre operators dependent on grid connections and third-party property leases.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: MBSB Research 认为 YTL Power 的 Bukit Kerayong 地块有潜力建设 4GW data centre campus
stories.summary_zh: MBSB Research认为YTL Power在Malaysia Bukit Kerayong的场地有潜力建设一个4GW的数据中心园区，基于该公司在Kulai的现有运营和计划向Sedenak Tech Park West的扩张。该研究报告维持对YTL Power的积极长期展望，其支撑在于数据中心增长以及电力和数字基础设施机会。
stories.why_zh: 一个4GW园区将跻身东南亚最大的整合数据中心开发之列，集中区域AI训练容量并重塑Johor相对于Singapore的竞争地位。YTL Power的集成发电和土地资产创造了垂直整合模式，对依赖电网连接和第三方物业租赁的独立数据中心运营商构成威胁。
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 30): MBSB Research remains positive on YTL Power International Bhd’s (KL:YTLPOWR) longer-term growth prospects, underpinned by the ramp-up of its data centre operations in Kulai, Johor, the planned expansion into Sedenak Tech Park West (STeP West), and rising opportunities in the power and digital infrastructure sectors.

The research firm also sees the group’s joint venture (JV) with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG) and Bumi Assets Sdn Bhd to develop land in Bukit Kerayong, Selangor, as a potential strategic milestone that could significantly expand its development pipeline over the longer term.

MBSB Research maintained its earnings forecasts and “buy” recommendation on YTL Power, with a sum-of-the-parts-derived target price of RM5.98, pending greater clarity on the proposed development.

"Our target price implies an FY2028 price-earnings ratio (PER) of 22.1 times. At its current share price, YTL Power is trading at 19.6 times FY2028 PER, which still offers an attractive entry point, in our view. We continue to favour YTL Power for its strategic expansion into data centres, which are emerging as a new growth driver for the group," the research firm said in a report on Friday.

YTL Power has entered into a JV with SD Guthrie and Bumi Assets to develop a 657.09ha freehold site at Bukit Kerayong Estate, which is currently used for oil palm cultivation.

The development will be undertaken through JV company Bukit Kerayong Industrial Developments Sdn Bhd (BKID). YTL Power and Bumi Assets each hold a 35% stake in BKID, while SD Guthrie owns the remaining 30%.

Although BKID has reportedly proposed an integrated industrial development for the site, MBSB Research does not rule out the possibility of a large-scale data centre campus being developed there, potentially exceeding the scale of YTL Power’s existing green data centre park in Kulai.

"Assuming approximately 500 acres are allocated for data centre development, we estimate that Bukit Kerayong could theoretically accommodate up to 4GW of capacity,” MBSB Research said.

YTL Power shares rose two sen or 0.38% to close at RM5.32 at Friday’s midday break, valuing the group at RM46.75 billion. The stock has gained 59.76% year to date.

stories.title: AI boom, soaring memory prices lift Japan's chip exports 41%
stories.summary: Japan's semiconductor exports surged 41% year-on-year, propelled by the global AI boom and sharply elevated memory chip prices. The growth underscores Japan's strengthening position in specialized chip components and materials critical to advanced AI hardware manufacturing.
stories.why_it_matters: Japan's export surge validates government industrial policy bets on reshoring semiconductor production, but concentrated gains in memory-dependent segments expose vulnerability to pricing cycles. Equipment and materials suppliers rather than integrated device manufacturers capture disproportionate value, suggesting Japan's AI chip leverage remains upstream rather than in finished GPU or accelerator design where margins concentrate.

stories.title: Keppel Energy, Sembcorp Utilities and Tuas Power to supply biomethane in pilot project
stories.summary: The sandbox will run for 15 years, with the companies expected to bring in their first supplies by end-2028

sources.name: The Business Times — Data Centres topic

stories.title_zh: Keppel Energy、Sembcorp Utilities和Tuas Power将在试点项目中供应生物甲烷
stories.content:
The sandbox will run for 15 years, with the companies expected to bring in their first supplies by end-2028

\[SINGAPORE\] Keppel Energy, Sembcorp Utilities and Tuas Power Generation have been appointed to import and supply biomethane as a renewable alternative to natural gas as part of a 300 megawatt (MW) pilot project.

Plans to set up the biomethane regulatory sandbox were first announced in October 2025 during the annual Singapore International Energy Week run by the Energy Market Authority.

The sandbox will run for 15 years, with the three power generation companies expected to bring in their first biomethane supplies by end-2028, said the Economic Development Board (EDB) on Friday (Oct 23).

Under the sandbox, the companies will import biomethane – that could generate up to 300 MW of power – from regional and international sources, and supply it to data centres and industrial manufacturers in Singapore, either as biomethane gas or as biomethane-derived electricity.

This capacity can supply the energy needs of around 600,000 public housing flats annually.

Of the 300 MW, Keppel Energy and Sembcorp Utilities are each expected to import and supply up to 120 MW of biomethane, while Tuas Power will supply the remainder.

“The initiative, the first of its kind in South-east Asia, will help Singapore explore biomethane as a decarbonisation pathway and pave the way for its wider adoption,” said EDB.

Unlike many emerging low-carbon fuels, biomethane is a direct drop-in replacement for fossil natural gas. This means it can utilise existing gas infrastructure and be consumed without modifications to equipment or industrial processes, making it one of the most practical near-term decarbonisation options available, it added.

“With natural gas accounting for around 95 per cent of Singapore’s electricity generation, biomethane offers a feasible pathway to reduce emissions from the power sector and heavily gas-dependent industries.”

In a separate statement, Keppel said that the imported biomethane will be handled with natural gas as an aggregated fuel portfolio for Keppel’s advanced combined cycle gas turbine plants on Jurong Island, as well as supplied to end-use customers.

The lower-carbon-intensity power can then be supplied to both industrial and advanced manufacturers, as well as data centre operators, including Keppel, which was recently provisionally awarded 50 MW of new data centre capacity.

Keppel was one of four operators granted approval to expand their data centre capacity in Singapore via a call for application.

“This will not only help Keppel fulfil its sustainability commitments, but also support other customers in meeting their needs for commercially competitive decarbonisation solutions,” said Keppel.

Janice Bong, managing director for the integrated power business under Keppel’s infrastructure division, said that the company’s integrated energy capabilities, experience in natural-gas sourcing and procurement, as well as cross-border power importation can provide a strong foundation to help develop Singapore’s biomethane pathway.

“By consolidating demand for biomethane, we can achieve economies of scale and optimise costs, enabling wider adoption and decarbonisation across multiple sectors,” she added.

Tuas Power’s senior vice-president for fuel management Ida Handojo said that the company’s experience in South-east Asia’s biomass market and logistics handling can support Singapore’s journey to develop the use of biomethane at scale.

“Agriculture is, and will continue to be, a significant economic activity in South-east Asia, offering substantial potential for biofuel sources,” she added.

Koh Chiap Khiong, president and CEO of gas and related services at Sembcorp Industries, said that the appointment reflects Sembcorp’s ability to bring together fuel supply, market demand and customer solutions at scale.

“We are well-positioned to help develop Singapore’s biomethane value chain and support the adoption of this emerging fuel,” he added. “In doing so, we can contribute to Singapore’s energy transition and help meet growing power demand from an increasingly digital and artificial intelligence-driven economy.”

stories.title: Melbourne overtakes Sydney in Australia data centre boom
stories.summary: Melbourne has surpassed Sydney in total forecast data centre capacity as Australia's development pipeline expanded by 5.2GW over six months, with faster planning approvals in Victoria driving the shift. The milestone reflects broader decentralization of Australian data centre investment beyond traditional east coast concentration.
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne's ascendance redistributes property value, talent pools and supply chain logistics within Australia's data centre ecosystem, creating new vendor ecosystems while potentially hollowing out Sydney's premium pricing power. Network latency to Asia-Pacific submarine cable landing points becomes a more critical site selection factor, advantaging Melbourne only if fibre backhaul investments keep pace with power and space commitments.
stories.title_zh: 墨尔本在澳大利亚数据中心热潮中超越悉尼
stories.summary_zh: 随着澳大利亚开发pipeline在六个月内扩张5.2GW，Melbourne在总forecast数据中心容量方面已超过Sydney，Victoria更快的规划审批推动了这一转变。这一里程碑反映了澳大利亚数据中心投资超越传统东海岸集中的更广泛分散化。
stories.why_zh: Melbourne的崛起重新分配了澳大利亚数据中心生态系统内的房地产价值、人才库和供应链物流，创造新的供应商生态系统，同时可能削弱Sydney的溢价定价能力。到亚太海底电缆登陆点的网络延迟成为更关键的选址因素，只有当光纤回程投资与电力和空间承诺保持同步时，Melbourne才能获得优势。
stories.content:
Fri, 30th Oct 2026 (Today)
Data Centres Australia has released the second edition of its Australian Data Centre Forecast Report, projecting national operational capacity will reach 3.9GW by 2030.

Produced with DC Byte, the study says Australia currently has 1.6GW of operational data centre capacity across 163 facilities tracked for the report. It also says the development pipeline has expanded sharply over the past six months, with 5.2GW added to the total forecast since April.

The figures point to a market that is still growing, but with notable shifts in where projects are advancing. While Sydney has long been the country's dominant hub, the latest numbers show Melbourne now surpasses Sydney in total forecast pipeline capacity.

Operational capacity rose by 0.1GW during the period covered by the report. Capacity under construction doubled from the previous period, split evenly between Sydney and Melbourne.

One of the clearest shifts was projects moving from early-stage planning into committed development. Melbourne recorded 1.2GW moving into the committed category, compared with 0.7GW in Sydney.

The report links that gap to planning and approvals. It says the movement in Melbourne may reflect faster approval processes under the Victorian Government's Development Facilitation Program than under the New South Wales State Significant Development process.

By contrast, Sydney recorded a fall in forecast pipeline volume. Its total pipeline dropped by 3.6GW, while early-stage capacity fell by 4.4GW.

The report says the decline is significant and likely reflects a combination of energy constraints, less certain policy approval timelines and recent policy announcements in New South Wales. It suggests investors and developers are becoming more selective about where they place large-scale digital infrastructure projects.

Melbourne moved in the opposite direction. Its total forecast pipeline increased by 1.7GW, with only a 0.3GW rise in early-stage projects, indicating much of the change came from schemes progressing through the development process rather than from a surge in newly announced sites.

This pattern may reflect faster approval times in Victoria and what the report describes as an "open for business" message from government. It also notes that later editions may show the effect of more recent policy changes.

### Beyond the main hubs

The data also points to a broader geographic spread of data centre development. Outside Sydney and Melbourne, the total forecast pipeline has increased from 19% to 31% over two years.

That shift includes early-stage projects in Queensland, Tasmania, South Australia and Western Australia. The trend suggests developers are looking beyond the two largest east coast markets as power availability, planning settings and land options shape site selection.

For state governments, that could bring both investment opportunities and pressure to prepare electricity networks, planning frameworks and industrial land for large data-intensive facilities. Data centres require significant, reliable energy supply, and several markets are now competing to attract projects linked to cloud computing and artificial intelligence workloads.

The report argues that policy settings are emerging as a major differentiator between states. Faster approvals and clearer planning signals appear to be helping Melbourne and a broader group of regional markets, while uncertainty around energy and regulation is weighing on Sydney's near-term pipeline.

### Demand drivers

The projected rise to 3.9GW of operational capacity by 2030 is tied to growing demand for cloud services and AI compute. These uses have become a central factor in data centre investment decisions, particularly as businesses and public sector bodies increase their use of digital services and machine learning tools.

Even so, the report indicates that supply growth will not depend on demand alone. Energy access, capital availability and national standards for AI infrastructure are among the factors that could shape the market over the coming months.

The latest forecast adds to evidence that Australia's data centre sector is entering a more dispersed and more policy-sensitive phase. Growth is continuing at the national level, but the balance between cities is shifting as developers respond to approval timelines, electricity constraints and government positioning.

With 97 additional facilities forecast by 2030, the sector remains on track for substantial expansion, though not evenly across the country. The report says Australia's data centre development footprint is expanding beyond Sydney and Melbourne, with the total forecast pipeline outside the two hubs rising from 19% to 31% over two years.

stories.title: Macquarie to acquire major shareholdings in South Korea's Gabia and KINX
stories.summary: Macquarie Asset Management (Macquarie), an Australian multinational investment banking and financial services group, is set to acquire controlling stakes in South Korean IT infrastructure provider Gabia and its subsidiary KINX after agreeing to buy shares from their major shareholders. According to a company press release, Macquarie will acquire the entire shareholdings of Gabia management, Align […]
stories.title_zh: 麦格理收购韩国Gabia和KINX主要股份
stories.content:
Macquarie Asset Management (Macquarie), an Australian multinational investment banking and financial services group, is set to acquire controlling stakes in South Korean IT infrastructure provider Gabia and its subsidiary KINX after agreeing to buy shares from their major shareholders.

According to a company press release, Macquarie will acquire the entire shareholdings of Gabia management, Align Partners, Miri Capital and Gumshoe Capital for KRW 53,000 (US$ 40) per Gabia share and KRW 190,000 (US$ 142) per KINX share through Macquarie Asia-Pacific Infrastructure Fund 4 (MAIF4).

“Korea is a key market for Macquarie, where we continue to see compelling opportunities as its digital economy continues to grow,” said Verena Lim, Co-Head of Asia-Pacific Infrastructure, Macquarie Asset Management and Asia CEO, Macquarie Group. “This transaction provides shareholders with an attractive opportunity to realise value, while establishing a simpler ownership structure to support the next phase of growth for Gabia and KINX.”

As part of the transaction, certain members of Gabia’s management team will contribute a portion of their existing shareholdings to the acquiring special purpose company (SPC) in exchange for an ownership interest, while retaining their management positions and continuing to oversee the businesses.

The proposed buyouts would consolidate the two companies under a simplified ownership structure, replacing their current dual-listed arrangement, subject to foreign investment and national security reviews by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources and merger clearance from the Korea Fair Trade Commission.

stories.title: Alphabet spells out more AI capex, China+1 doesn't add up
stories.summary: Oracle plans to shift its enterprise software pricing model from traditional seat-based subscriptions to usage-based billing for embedded AI tasks, aiming to capture more revenue from existing customer deployments. The strategy accompanies heavy investments in cloud infrastructure to support AI workloads across its software portfolio.
stories.why_it_matters: Usage-based AI billing transforms Oracle's relationship with customers from predictable recurring revenue to variable consumption models, creating revenue volatility but aligning costs with actual value extraction. Enterprise buyers must rebuild cost forecasting frameworks, while Oracle's cloud infrastructure investments now face direct pressure to convert software usage into infrastructure utilization.
stories.title_zh: Alphabet宣布更多AI capex，China+1策略难以成立
stories.summary_zh: Oracle计划将其企业软件定价模式从传统的seat-based订阅转向embedded AI任务的usage-based计费，旨在从现有客户部署中获取更多收入。该战略伴随着对cloud infrastructure的重投资，以支持其软件组合中的AI工作负载。
stories.why_zh: 基于使用量的AI计费将Oracle与客户的关系从可预测的经常性收入转变为可变消费模式，创造收入波动性，但使成本与实际价值提取保持一致。企业买家必须重建成本预测框架，而Oracle的cloud infrastructure投资现在面临将软件使用量转化为基础设施利用率的直接压力。
stories.content:
Hello from Yifan in Silicon Valley. I hope everyone (in the Northern Hemisphere) is enjoying the falling leaves and sweater season.

Wall Street got a proper scare from Alphabet's earnings before Halloween. On Wednesday, Google's parent company reported solid third-quarter revenue growth, with record sales for the cloud business unit. But its shares plunged more than 10% at one point during extended trading, despite all signs indicating that more people and companies are now using Google's AI services and even its in-house AI chips.

After several years of tech companies pouring billions and billions of dollars into AI, revenue growth alone is no longer enough to impress the market. Google's spending of $51.4 billion in capex for AI infrastructure buildout in three months and ending the quarter with negative free cash flow of $9 billion turned out to be a warning sign for many, rather than a boost to confidence in continued AI investment.

Samsung Electronics got a similar cold shoulder from the market after its earnings report Thursday. Despite the South Korean semiconductor giant saying it became the first global technology company to top 100 trillion won in quarterly operating profit, thanks to continued demand for memory chips amid the AI buildout, its shares slumped following the earnings report.

Investors are now growing increasingly worried about the massive spending on AI by companies such as Google and are starting to demand proper returns here and now, not in five years.

As Wall Street awaits this week for other U.S. Big Tech companies to release their third-quarter earnings and future AI investment guidance, we are seeing similar reality checks on AI across global markets, including in China, where AI stocks have fallen sharply in recent weeks due to similar concerns about the profitability of AI.

Tech illuminati such as Elon Musk have long criticized the public market for being shortsighted and overlooking the long-term benefits of investing in technology that's expensive to build.

But it has been almost four years since the ChatGPT-led AI boom began, so how patient should the market be?

As if it were not jittery enough, the U.S. midterm elections next week are casting another shadow over AI trades. More U.S. voters are turning against AI and data centers than ever before.

Around 40 local ballot measures nationwide on data center development will go to a vote on Nov. 3. The implications will reach far beyond the U.S., as the entire Asian tech supply chain, from Taiwanese server makers to South Korean chipmakers, eagerly awaits the results.

## **China+1 not adding up for PC makers**

Leading PC makers, including HP of the U.S. and Asus and Acer of Taiwan, are combating soaring component costs by shifting some production from Thailand and Vietnam back to China and using a new generation of contract manufacturers, Nikkei Asia's **Lauly Li** and **Cheng Ting-Fang** report.

Multiple sources told Nikkei Asia that the PC makers are seeking greater manufacturing efficiency as their bill of materials rises, with demand from AI causing acute memory and storage shortages.

The shift marks a partial reversal, for now, of the global tech supply chain's "China+1" diversification strategy, which moved some production from China to other Southeast Asian countries as U.S.-China tensions led to trade restrictions.

The PC makers are now turning to lesser-known Chinese contractors whose larger rivals have become increasingly occupied with higher-margin orders for AI data center servers. Dell of the U.S., the third-largest PC maker behind Lenovo and HP, is also evaluating a similar move, according to the sources.

Industry insiders say China remains the best option for making computers, with its experienced workforce, lower prices and a complete supply chain ecosystem that can offer full access to components.

## **Could Toyota be the world's biggest robot maker?**

Toyota is setting its sights on becoming a global robotics powerhouse, as the world's largest car manufacturer modernizes production lines to compete with China and diversify beyond the auto industry, write **Harry Dempsey** and **David Keohane** from the FT's Tokyo bureau.

Its top executives have been drumming up global investor interest for its robotics strategy, including plans to deploy 400,000 robots as part of a $6.4 billion annual investment to automate factories and establish a dedicated robotics team.

"I think that Toyota could be the biggest humanoid robot company on the planet - they just need to get after it," said Carl Vine at M&G, a Toyota investor.

The auto market is offering less room for growth, and the price tag for a humanoid robot is likely to be significantly higher than the cost of a new car. Goldman Sachs analysts estimate that Toyota could capture 3% to 8% of the humanoid market by 2035.

But that might not be enough to boost Toyota's overall growth. "It's the kind of thing that's rewarded if Toyota's core car business is doing well and dismissed as a distraction if the car business is suffering," one Asia-based Toyota investor said.

## **China's AI stocks in freefall**

Mounting concerns over the profitability of AI are weighing on Chinese stock markets, despite homegrown AI being crucial to the country's strategy of technological self-reliance, Nikkei Asia's **Kensaku Ihara** and **Anne Chan** write.

The CSI Artificial Intelligence Index, which tracks major Chinese AI-related companies, has fallen nearly 40% from its June peak, led by state-backed semiconductor companies such as Cambricon Technologies, often dubbed "China's Nvidia."

China Merchants Securities International has warned investors of increasing volatility in AI-related stocks, advising them to "pay greater attention to defensive stocks in the sector."

Concerns about the earnings prospects of AI players are growing in China, following a sell-off of U.S. AI stocks driven by questions over whether their massive infrastructure investments will pay off.

## **A stellar sevenfold profit increase for SK Hynix**

SK Hynix's third-quarter operating profit soared more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won ($62.9 billion) from a year ago, driven by strong demand for its advanced memory chips critical to AI computing, as global hyperscalers increase investment in servers, data centers and other AI infrastructure.

The world's second-largest memory chipmaker said on Wednesday that revenue more than quadrupled to 104.6 trillion won in the three months through September. The South Korean company's net profit more than tripled to 39.8 trillion won, Nikkei Asia's **Kim Jaewon** reports.

The stellar performance of SK Hynix, a key supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips to U.S. chipmaker Nvidia, comes as investors express concern through volatile stock markets about massive AI investments by major tech companies such as Google, Meta and OpenAI.

On Thursday, Samsung Electronics, another major memory chip supplier, also reported record third-quarter earnings. Its semiconductor unit's operating profit surpassed 100 trillion won. But rising memory chip prices backfired on its smartphone business, as higher manufacturing costs led the unit to post an operating loss of 0.6 trillion won.

stories.title: DayOne, Blue Whale to study Singapore virtual power plant
stories.summary: The study could ease peak load pressure on Singapore's grid as AI demand rises, while testing whether data centres can help balance power use.
stories.title_zh: DayOne与Blue Whale研究新加坡虚拟电厂
stories.content:
Fri, 30th Oct 2026 (Today)
DayOne Data Centres and Blue Whale Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding to study a distributed virtual power plant in Singapore. The proposed project would link battery storage at DayOne's planned SG1 data centre with batteries at other commercial and industrial sites.

The study will examine whether a distributed battery energy storage network can be coordinated in real time so multiple sites operate as a single resource for the electricity grid. It will focus on linking storage at the SG1 facility with suitable third-party locations.

The plan reflects growing pressure on electricity systems as demand from artificial intelligence and cloud computing rises. Data centre operators and grid managers are looking for ways to make better use of existing power infrastructure, especially during periods of peak demand.

A distributed virtual power plant, or VPP, typically combines energy assets at different locations and manages them through software and control systems. In this case, the aim is to pool battery storage across several sites so electricity drawn from the grid can be adjusted when needed.

According to the companies, the approach could help reduce strain on the grid at key moments and may limit the need for some network upgrades that would otherwise be required to meet peak demand. It would also test whether a data centre can act as an anchor site in a wider energy management network.

### Study scope

The initial work is expected to include a joint front-end engineering design study covering storage configuration, safety, metering and telemetry, controls, operational safeguards, and possible arrangements with participating commercial and industrial facilities.

The companies also plan to engage with authorities and market stakeholders to understand technical requirements and the conditions for taking part in relevant market schemes. Those discussions are expected to address how a distributed system of this kind would fit within Singapore's existing electricity market rules.

Another part of the assessment will examine potential participation in Singapore's Demand Response and Interruptible Load programmes. These programmes are designed to encourage businesses to cut electricity use during periods of market stress and grid contingencies to support system reliability.

That element of the study will depend on applicable market rules and regulatory approvals. It also highlights a broader question facing data centre operators in Singapore and other constrained markets: how to add digital infrastructure without placing disproportionate pressure on power networks.

### Data centre role

DayOne is based in Singapore and operates data centres across Asia Pacific and Europe. Its footprint spans 10 markets, including Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Japan, Hong Kong, Finland and Spain.

DayOne's SG1 development is set to become the anchor asset in the proposed study. By connecting that site's battery storage to systems installed elsewhere, the partners want to test whether a cluster of commercial and industrial assets can respond to grid conditions in a coordinated way.

Blue Whale Energy, also based in Singapore, specialises in battery energy storage systems and VPP aggregation services. Its role in the study will centre on the technical, operational and commercial arrangements needed to combine multiple battery assets into one coordinated platform.

Jamie Khoo, chief executive officer of DayOne, framed the work as part of a wider debate about the infrastructure that underpins digital growth.

"Singapore's digital economy depends not only on computing infrastructure but also on the physical systems that support it, including energy. We believe data centers should play an active role in strengthening the broader power ecosystem they rely on and creating long-term value," Khoo said.

"Through this collaboration with Blue Whale Energy, we are exploring how a distributed VPP anchored at a data center could support greater grid flexibility alongside the continued growth of digital infrastructure," he said.

Blue Whale Energy said the project will test whether a central data centre site can be combined with other facilities in a way that creates a workable commercial and operational model.

"Coordinated energy storage could create value by bringing together an anchor data center and suitable commercial and industrial sites," said Gabriel Lim, founder and chief executive officer of Blue Whale Energy.

"Through this MOU with DayOne, we will assess the technical, operational, and commercial arrangements required for a distributed VPP that shows what that future could look like, starting here in Singapore," Lim said.

stories.title: Australian DC pipeline reaches 26.8GW as development shifts beyond Sydney
stories.summary: Australia's total data centre pipeline has expanded to 26.8GW, with Melbourne now surpassing Sydney in forecast capacity due to faster approval timelines. The report from DCA and DC Byte highlights a geographic diversification trend, with an increasing proportion of projects planned for markets outside the two traditional east coast hubs.
stories.why_it_matters: The shift in Australia's data centre geography reshapes where power, land and fibre investments flow, benefiting Melbourne and secondary markets while pressuring Sydney's dominance. Developers and local governments in regional areas gain leverage, but infrastructure readiness outside established hubs will determine which projects actually reach completion.
stories.title_zh: 澳大利亚数据中心管道容量达26.8GW，开发向悉尼以外地区转移
stories.summary_zh: 澳大利亚的数据中心总pipeline已达到26.8GW，由于审批速度更快，Melbourne目前在forecast capacity方面已超过Sydney。DCA和DC Byte的报告强调了地理多元化趋势，越来越多项目计划部署在两个传统东海岸hub之外的市场。
stories.why_zh: 澳大利亚数据中心地理格局的转变正在重塑电力、土地和光纤投资的流向，使Melbourne和二级市场受益，同时对Sydney的主导地位构成压力。偏远地区的开发商和地方政府获得了更大的议价能力，但 established hubs 之外的基础设施准备情况将决定哪些项目能够真正完工。
stories.content:
Australia’s data centre development pipeline has grown by 5.2GW in six months, with Melbourne overtaking Sydney in total forecast capacity and projects outside the two largest markets accounting for a rising share of planned development, according to a new report from Data Centres Australia (DCA) and DC Byte.

The **Australian Data Centre Forecast Report** puts the national pipeline at 26.8GW, up from 21.6GW in April. However, the report distinguishes between projects at different stages of development, with a significant portion of the total still in early-stage planning and subject to uncertainty.

Australia has 1.6GW of operational data centre capacity across 163 facilities tracked by DC Byte. The report forecasts operational capacity will reach 3.9GW by 2030, up from the 3.2GW forecast in the previous edition.

The report’s methodology assesses project viability rather than treating announced plans or grid connection applications as evidence that capacity will be delivered. It accounts for factors including land, power, permits, developer track records, construction timelines and customer ramp-up schedules.

“Capacity under construction has doubled since our April report and more capacity has moved from early stage to committed, demonstrating continued demand in the market,” said Belinda Dennett, CEO of Data Centres Australia (*above*).

### Melbourne overtakes Sydney in pipeline capacity

Melbourne’s total forecast pipeline has increased by 1.7GW since April to 10.7GW, exceeding Sydney’s 7.8GW. Sydney’s pipeline has fallen by 3.6GW over the same period, from 11.4GW.

The report attributes the contrasting movements partly to differences in energy availability, policy settings and approval processes. It suggests that Victoria’s Development Facilitation Program may have helped move projects from early-stage planning into the committed category more quickly than the NSW State Significant Development process.

Melbourne recorded a 1.2GW increase in committed capacity, compared with 700MW in Sydney. Melbourne’s early-stage capacity rose by 300MW to 7.8GW, while Sydney’s fell by 4.4GW to 4.2GW.

DCA said Sydney’s reduction was likely to reflect a combination of announced energy constraints, less certain approval timelines and recent policy announcements. It said Victoria’s increase may reflect faster approvals and the state government’s previous “open for business” message, although recent policy changes could affect future forecasts.

The report notes that the Victorian Government has announced new policies for data centres, along with an apparent pause on approvals in the lead-up to the November 2026 state election. It says its next forecast may show whether this has a material impact.

“The analysis shows pronounced growth in the data centre pipeline in Victoria over the last six months, likely attributable to the state government’s efforts to attract investment,” Dennett said. “We expect recent changes in policy may have an impact on whether this continues.”

The report’s figures are based on data current to 30 September 2026.

### More development outside traditional hubs

The share of forecast pipeline capacity located outside Sydney and Melbourne has increased from 19 percent in the third quarter of 2024 to 31 percent in September 2026. The report includes early-stage projects in Queensland, Tasmania, South Australia and Western Australia, alongside regional developments in NSW and Victoria.

DCA expects the trend to continue as energy constraints, policy decisions and demand from AI and neocloud operators influence site selection. DCA said new workloads such as AI and neoclouds may bring different siting requirements.

“We are also seeing current energy constraints and different policy approaches influence customer and operator decisions,” Dennett said.

The report identifies the availability of energy and capital, along with the Federal Government’s proposed AI infrastructure standards, as factors to watch over the next six months.

### Pipeline growth remains weighted towards early-stage projects

Of the 26.8GW national pipeline, 19.6GW is classified as early stage, up from 16.8GW in April. A further 5.2GW is committed, compared with 3.1GW six months earlier, while capacity under construction has doubled from 200MW to 400MW.

DC Byte defines committed projects as those for which it has high confidence of eventual delivery, generally because key requirements such as land, power and permits have been secured, or because the project is being developed by an operator with a reliable track record. Early-stage projects have yet to secure all the elements required for development and may not proceed.

The distinction is significant given that 52 projects in the national pipeline have announced capacity exceeding 100MW, compared with four operational data centres of that size.

The report forecasts operational capacity will rise from approximately 1.8GW at the end of 2026 to 2.3GW in 2027, 2.7GW in 2028 and 3.4GW in 2029, reaching 3.9GW by 2030.

Dennett said Australia remained an attractive market for data centre development, pointing to its industry ecosystem and large-scale renewable energy generation. She said credible forecasting was needed to inform policy and infrastructure planning as the market grows.

stories.title: Quantum DC cancels Australian data center community meeting over "credible bomb threat"
stories.summary: The proposed gigawatt-scale has seen local pushback
stories.title_zh: Quantum DC因"可信炸弹威胁"取消澳大利亚数据中心社区会议
stories.content:
A drop-in meeting for a proposed gigawatt data center has been canceled after the company behind it claimed it faced a "credible" bomb threat.

Developer Quantum DC is looking to build the Tungkillo Compute and Energy Hub, a large-scale data center and power campus that could total 1.2GW at full build-out.

Should the Adelaide, Australia, project be approved, the company anticipates the first stage will commence operations in 2028, with the full development completed by 2031.

The company has not previously built or operated data centers.

The project has faced mounting opposition from locals and farmers, who claim that the 220-acre development would impact the natural environment, livestock, and the dark sky reserve. Project documents state that facility construction is expected to require 150 million to 250 million liters of water, with an annual water demand of about 20 million liters once operational.

Quantum DC has sought to use South Australia’s Essential Infrastructure assessment process, which would provide a 15-day public submission period.

The company looked to address some of these local concerns with a drop-in session.

"Unfortunately, due to a credible bomb threat made, we have had to cancel this community drop-in session in the interest of safety," a note from the company said. "This has been reported to SA Police.

"We will share more information very soon about future opportunities for engagement. Please see quantumdc.com.au."

Quantum DC chief executive Alby Tomassi told 7news: “We are extremely disappointed that we were forced to postpone this afternoon’s community drop-in session after a credible bomb threat was received.

“Public safety must always take priority, and we had no choice but to make this decision."

*DCD* has contacted Tomassi for more details on the incident.

stories.title: Google share price slumps as AI data center build-out drives $9bn negative cashflow
stories.summary: Alphabet's share price declined sharply after the company reported $9 billion in negative free cash flow driven by accelerated AI data centre construction spending. The search and cloud giant affirmed that capital expenditure will continue at planned levels despite investor concerns about near-term returns on infrastructure investments.
stories.why_it_matters: Alphabet's cash burn trajectory tests whether equity markets will continue funding hyperscale AI infrastructure buildouts without immediate revenue proof points, potentially tightening financing conditions for the entire sector. If Google cannot demonstrate workload monetization soon, smaller cloud providers and data centre developers may face higher capital costs or delayed project commitments.
stories.title_zh: Google股价下跌，AI数据中心建设导致90亿美元负现金流
stories.summary_zh: Alphabet的股价在公司报告因加速AI数据中心建设支出导致90亿美元负自由现金流后大幅下跌。这家搜索和云巨头确认，尽管投资者对基础设施投资的近期回报表示担忧，capex将按原计划水平继续。
stories.why_zh: Alphabet的现金消耗轨迹正在检验股票市场是否会在没有即时收入验证点的情况下继续资助hyperscale AI基础设施建设，可能收紧整个行业的融资条件。如果Google无法很快证明工作负载的货币化，较小的云提供商和数据中心开发商可能面临更高的资本成本或延迟的项目承诺。
stories.content:
Google’s parent company, Alphabet, saw its share price dip sharply after it reported a surprise negative cash flow of $9 billion, largely due to its investments in digital infrastructure.

The company’s earnings for the three months to the end of September showed its revenue grew 25 percent to $127.58 billion, slightly less than the expected $128.22 billion.

Negative cash flow, which had been expected to be around $2.7 billion, came in at $9.01 billion. CFO Anat Ashkenazi told investors that the larger-than-expected number was “driven by our investments in capex.”

Google has been investing heavily in its data center infrastructure to support its AI products, and has started selling its custom-designed TPU AI chips to third parties.

It is working with Blackstone to create a US-based cloud platform offering its TPUs, named Crux AI. Neocloud Fluidstack is also known to be deploying TPUs for Anthropic in a series of Google-backed deals.

This week, it was revealed that TPUs would be available on Oracle’s OCI cloud platform from next year. Oracle’s Karan Batta told *DCD* that the deal is a “multi-year, multi-gigawatt” partnership.

All this requires a lot of money up front, and Google spent $51.36 billion in capex in the last quarter, while maintaining its guidance for annual spending of up to $205 billion in 2027, with $300 billion to come in 2028.

The company’s share price slumped as much as 10 percent in after-hours trading, ahead of the markets opening on Thursday.

Ashkenazi added that the company’s cash flow had been “negatively impacted by the buildup of inventory for TPU system sales” as well as a $5.2 billion cash payment for a 2018 European Commission fine over breaching EC antitrust regulations with its Android mobile operating system.

There was better news in its Google Cloud division, where quarterly revenue grew 108 percent Year-on-Year, to $30.7 billion.

Google's results were published on the same day that rival hyperscaler Microsoft announced its results, and saw its share price climb as a result. Microsoft reported positive free cash flow of $18.63 billion, despite being heavily invested in its own AI infrastructure build-out, with capex of $45.2 billion.

stories.title: Microsoft thinks its data centers can last for 25 years, reports strong cloud earnings and lower capex
stories.summary: Microsoft has extended the accounting useful life of its data centre facilities to 25 years, reflecting confidence in long-term asset durability and reduced obsolescence risk from modular infrastructure designs. The change accompanies first-time separate disclosure of Azure revenue and lower-than-expected capital expenditure in the latest quarter.
stories.why_it_matters: Extended depreciation schedules improve reported earnings and free cash flow, giving Microsoft financial flexibility to sustain competitive pricing pressure or accelerate AI infrastructure deployment. For the broader industry, Microsoft's 25-year assumption sets a benchmark that may pressure auditors and competitors to justify shorter facility lifespans, potentially triggering accounting policy convergence across hyperscale operators.
stories.title_zh: Microsoft认为其数据中心可使用25年，报告强劲云收入和更低capex
stories.summary_zh: Microsoft已将其数据中心设施的会计使用寿命延长至25年，反映了对长期资产耐用性和模块化基础设施设计降低过时风险的信心。这一变化伴随着Azure收入的首次单独披露以及最新季度低于预期的capex。
stories.why_zh: 延长折旧时间表改善了报告收益和自由现金流，使Microsoft具有财务灵活性来维持竞争性定价压力或加速AI基础设施部署。对于整个行业，Microsoft的25年假设设定了一个基准，可能促使审计师和竞争对手证明更短的设施寿命，从而触发hyperscale运营商之间的会计政策趋同。
stories.content:
Microsoft believes its data centers can last for up to 25 years.

The company revealed in its Q1 2027 earnings call that it is extending the expected useful life of office buildings and data centers in its estate from 15 to 25 years. CFO Amy Hood said this reflected Microsoft's "operating history and expected use of these assets.”

It is thought Microsoft currently has access to some 12GW of data center capacity.

CEO Satya Nadella told investors on the earnings call that his firm continues “to get more from the infrastructure we already have by optimizing across the data center design, silicon systems, software, and models.”

He added: For example, we increased the throughput for Copilot workloads by over 50 percent quarter-over-quarter. We continue to scale our fleet with the latest innovations from Nvidia, AMD, alongside our own Maia systems.”

Research from the Uptime Institute published in 2024 found that data centers typically operate for 10-15 years, with the average mean lifespan of a data center sitting at 11.3 years.

Extending the useful life of data centers is also a handy accounting move for Microsoft, as it can spread the cost of multi-billion-dollar facilities over a longer time period.

The quarter saw Microsoft disclose the revenue of its Azure cloud platform for the first time, revealing it generated $33.2 billion in revenue in the last quarter.

The figure represents a 48 percent Year-on-Year (YoY) increase, and means Azure was responsible for 36 percent of the company’s revenue in the three months to the end of September.

During the period, Microsoft brought 24 new data centers online, but the company also reported lower-than-expected capex because a number of deals with neoclouds have been delayed.

Microsoft’s Agents and Infra division, which includes its Azure cloud platform and AI tools, made $76.8 billion, up 25 percent YoY. Microsoft introduced Agents and Infra as a business section in its reporting in September as part of a move towards "full transparency of quarterly revenue across each of our key businesses.”

Nadella said: “We are building against a growing book of business with a fungible fleet that allows us to dynamically allocate capacity to the highest value opportunities across compute, data, Foundry \[its AI developer platform\], and \[AI assistant\] Copilot.

“Accelerating demand led to us adding 24 new data centers across five continents this quarter. We are bringing capacity online faster, reducing dock-to-live times by about 20 percent quarter-over-quarter for new GB300s in our biggest regions, which make up the majority of the GPU deployments.”

Microsoft capex for the quarter was $45.2 billion, lower than the expected $50.7 billion. It said this was a result of some of the companies it works with for AI cloud services failing to provide data center capacity on time. As a result, Microsoft is estimating annual capex for 2027 of $170 billion, down from the previous estimate of $175 billion. The company has signed deals with a wide range of neoclouds, including CoreWeave, Nscale, Lambda, Iren, and Nebius.

stories.title: Nvidia, AMD invest $4 billion in Meta for AI buildout
stories.summary: Nvidia and AMD are collectively committing $4 billion to Meta's AI infrastructure expansion through strategic investments. Meta simultaneously announced plans to raise $97.5 billion via an equity offering to fund additional AI investments, signaling massive capital deployment across the AI supply chain.
stories.why_it_matters: Chip vendors becoming direct financial backers of their largest customer deepens interdependencies in the AI ecosystem and risks distorting competitive dynamics. For rivals without similar supplier relationships, Meta's fortified balance sheet raises the capital barrier to competing at hyperscale AI training and inference.
stories.title_zh: NVIDIA、AMD 向 Meta 投资 40 亿美元用于 AI 基础设施建设
stories.summary_zh: Nvidia和AMD将通过战略投资共同向Meta的AI基础设施扩张投入40亿美元。Meta同时宣布计划通过股权融资筹集975亿美元以资助额外的AI投资，标志着整个AI供应链的大规模资本部署。
stories.why_zh: 芯片供应商成为其最大客户的直接财务支持者，加深了AI生态系统中的相互依赖关系，并可能扭曲竞争动态。对于没有类似供应商关系的竞争对手而言，Meta得到强化的资产负债表提高了在hyperscale AI训练和推理领域竞争的资本门槛。
stories.content:
Nvidia and AMD are investing a combined $4 billion in Meta, deepening their relationships with the hyperscaler as it expands its AI infrastructure footprint. Meta plans to raise $97.5 billion through an equity offering to support its continued investment in AI infrastructure.Nvidia announced a $3 billion investment and Meta intends to deploy more Nvidia infrastructure. This includes its Vera Rubin platform and Vera CPUs for next-generation agents, as well as Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4 DPUs.Nvidia and Meta will also deepen their collaboration on Meta’s Muse models and agents, which leverage Nvidia infrastructure. The companies are considering additional work involving Nvidia OpenShell Reference Architecture to strengthen AI agent security.AMD committed $1 billion, highlighting new milestones in its partnership with Meta. Initial AMD Helios rack-scale systems have been installed and are being tested by Meta ahead of a broader deployment.Meta has deployed millions of AMD Epyc processors and is a lead customer for its sixth-generation Epyc CPUs. According to AMD, Epyc chips support the dedicated computing environments behind Meta’s Muse personal AI agent.Meta is also using AMD Instinct GPUs for training, ranking, and recommendation workloads. It plans to deploy a custom AMD Instinct GPU optimized for its own workloads, AMD said.Analysts view these investments as efforts by Nvidia and AMD to secure long-term AI infrastructure business with major hyperscalers. Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said this continues both companies’ investments in strategic hyperscalers to drive greater platform adoption.Brendan Burke, research director at Futurum Group, noted that both Nvidia and AMD view Meta’s AI agent strategy as promising. He added that Meta’s progress in training models and advancing its personal AI agent strategy suggests it has become a viable frontier AI lab.

- AI & Compute Infrastructure
- 1 min Read

# Nvidia, AMD invest $4 billion in Meta for AI buildout

Nvidia and AMD are investing a combined $4 billion in Meta to support its expanding AI infrastructure. Meta plans to raise $97.5 billion through an equity offering for further AI investments.

- Published On Oct 29, 2026 at 05:30 PM IST

## Highlights

- Nvidia and AMD are investing a combined $4 billion in Meta's AI infrastructure.
- Meta plans to deploy Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and BlueField-4 DPUs.
- AMD's Helios rack-scale systems are being tested by Meta, which uses Epyc CPUs and Instinct GPUs.
- Investments reflect chipmakers' efforts to secure long-term AI infrastructure business with hyperscalers.

stories.title: Labor to ban AI data centres in suburban Australia
stories.summary: Australia's Labor party has proposed prohibiting AI data centre construction in suburban areas, redirecting development to industrial zones with adequate power and cooling infrastructure. The policy aims to address community concerns about noise, visual impact, and strain on local electricity networks.
stories.why_it_matters: Zoning restrictions would fragment Australia's already constrained development pipeline, lengthening approval timelines and potentially concentrating power demand in fewer, larger industrial precincts. Suburban landholders and smaller colocation operators lose flexibility, while industrial zone property owners and transmission network planners gain predictable demand clusters but face accelerated upgrade deadlines.
stories.title_zh: 工党拟禁止在澳大利亚郊区建设AI数据中心
stories.summary_zh: 澳大利亚Labor党提议禁止在郊区建设AI数据中心，将开发重新导向拥有充足电力和冷却基础设施的工业区。该政策旨在解决社区对噪音、视觉影响和地方电网压力的担忧。
stories.why_zh: 分区限制将分化澳大利亚本已受限的开发pipeline，延长审批时间，并可能将电力需求集中在更少、更大的工业区。郊区土地所有者和较小的colocation运营商失去灵活性，而工业区物业所有者和输电网规划者获得可预测的需求集群，但面临加速的升级期限。
stories.content:
The Albanese government will ban artificial intelligence data centres from being built near homes and recreational facilities amid growing voter backlash over the massive industrial sites cropping up in inner Sydney and Melbourne suburbs.

Labor has also changed plans for a controversial copyright licensing regime that would have allowed tech giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic to scrape internet content freely without compensating creators.

The potential expansion would extend the company's footprint beyond its existing east coast and Singapore markets.
stories.why_it_matters: AirTrunk's westward move tests whether Western Australia's energy resources can overcome the latency and connectivity disadvantages of operating far from major population centres. Success would validate a new model for APAC data centre siting using industrial energy hubs, while failure would reinforce the concentration of capacity in established corridors.
stories.title_zh: AirTrunk考虑在新天然气枢纽建设西澳首个数据中心

stories.why_zh: AirTrunk向西扩张将检验Western Australia的能源资源能否克服远离主要人口中心所带来的延迟和连接性劣势。成功将验证一种利用工业能源hub的APAC数据中心选址新模式，而失败则将强化容量集中在established corridors的现状。

stories.title: South Korea's FuriosaAI quadruples value to US$2.9 bil in Nvidia chase
stories.summary: South Korean artificial intelligence (AI) chip start-up FuriosaAI quadrupled its valuation to US$2.9 billion (RM11.8 billion) in a fresh funding round, bolstering its bid to challenge the likes of Nvidia Corp.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: 韩国 FuriosaAI 在追赶 Nvidia 的过程中估值翻两番至 29 亿美元
stories.content:
(Oct 29): South Korean artificial intelligence (AI) chip start-up FuriosaAI quadrupled its valuation to US$2.9 billion (RM11.8 billion) in a fresh funding round, bolstering its bid to challenge the likes of Nvidia Corp.

The Seoul-based upstart said on Thursday it raised US$620 million in a Series D round from investors including US-based Infinitum Partners. South Korea’s National Growth Fund contributed US$280 million and international investors US$110 million, with Jericho Capital, Worldline Capital, Singapore’s QUDA Capital and Abu Dhabi-based NeoFort Holding among backers.

Investors are hunting for alternatives for Nvidia chips that dominate AI data centres, seeking more energy-efficient silicon. That shift centres on inference — generating outputs from trained AI models — which is emerging as one of the industry’s primary cost battlegrounds as rising demand boosts power needs.

Founded in 2017, FuriosaAI began mass production of RNGD — pronounced “renegade” — chips in January and is working with Broadcom Inc on a third-generation accelerator targeting large-scale AI infrastructure. The start-up is betting that its chip architecture, designed to minimise energy-intensive data movement, will help it gain ground in the Nvidia-led market. Its previous round last year valued the company at US$735 million.

FuriosaAI is engaged with a large number of customers in the Asia-Pacific region and Middle East, chief executive officer June Paik said in an interview on Bloomberg Television on Thursday. “We see strong demand and opportunities as we are scaling our business globally.”

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co is producing 20,000 RNGD accelerators this year, with the South Korean start-up aiming to more than double output to over 40,000 units in 2027. Samsung SDS, LG Group and South Korean AI start-up Upstage are among those that are using the chips.

Existing backers Naver Corp, Korea Development Bank, DSC Investment, Nextrans and Kakao Investment also joined the financing round, while the Export-Import Bank of Korea made its first direct start-up investment in FuriosaAI.

stories.title_zh: 数据中心负载转移可将峰值电力需求降低 0.6%
stories.content:
Global data centres are expected to achieve only a 0.1-0.6 per cent reduction in peak power demand across major markets by 2030 through load shifting, according to a new analysis by energy think tank Ember. The report, released on October 29, estimates that only about 3 per cent of global data centre capacity will be capable of shifting electricity consumption by 2030.This limited potential for load shifting comes as data centre operators explore flexible electricity consumption to manage rising demand and ease pressure on grid infrastructure. About 87 per cent of global data centre capacity in 2030 is expected to support cloud services, enterprise IT operations, and AI inference.These workloads typically require continuous operations or near-instant responses, which limits the scope to defer electricity consumption to off-peak periods. AI training facilities offer greater flexibility because some computing tasks can be scheduled or temporarily interrupted.However, AI training is expected to account for a relatively small share of global data centre capacity, limiting the overall potential for load shifting. Ember examined nine major markets, including Texas, California, New York, Ireland, the UK, Germany, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Singapore.In Ireland and Malaysia, data centres could account for around a quarter of peak electricity demand by 2030, making their consumption patterns particularly significant for grid operators. Ember cautioned that its estimates are indicative and based on limited available data.Onsite electricity generation and battery storage could provide substantially greater relief to power grids than shifting computing workloads, the report said. Onsite generation allows data centres to continue operating while reducing the electricity they draw from the grid during peak demand periods.A case study of two large data centres in Texas found that switching to onsite power generation could reduce peak grid demand by as much as 2.7 gigawatts (GW). Load shifting at the same facilities could reduce peak demand by about 0.55 GW, indicating onsite generation could deliver nearly five times the peak demand reduction. Ember flagged the growing use of natural gas-based generation by data centre developers seeking reliable electricity supplies, potentially increasing dependence on fossil fuels.

# Data centre load shifting to cut peak power demand by 0.6 per cent

A new Ember report indicates that global data centres may achieve only a 0.1-0.6 per cent reduction in peak power demand through load shifting by 2030. Onsite power generation is projected to offer more substantial relief to power grids than shifting computing workloads.

- Published On Oct 29, 2026 at 01:15 PM IST

## Highlights

- Ember projects data centre load shifting to cut peak demand by 0.1-0.6 per cent by 2030.
- Only 3 per cent of global data centre capacity is expected to support load shifting.
- Onsite generation could reduce peak grid demand by 2.7 GW in a Texas case study.
- AI training offers more flexibility for load shifting than continuous AI inference.
